title: a register row cannot say WHICH BUILD it describes, so the open set silently mixes main with the shipped tag
body:
**A register row says what is broken and never says WHICH BUILD it is broken in.** Rows accumulate against `main` while readers, and every instrument, stand on a published tag. Nothing in the record distinguishes the two, so the register cannot be partitioned by build without re-driving it row by row.

**Driven, not inferred.** Ten open rows were run against the published tag -- `intent 3.0.0 (80d8b2ca)`, installed as an unlinked keg, in a tree that binary initialised -- and none of them describes it:

    0016 0067 0079 0122 0137 0145 0146 0149 0171 0189

Each is named with its refutation in `docs/known-defects.md` under *Recorded against v3.0.0 and NOT present in it*. **Ten is a floor, not a total.** That page is the driven set by construction; rows needing a condition it cannot create from a fresh project -- a migrated estate, an installed skill, a running daemon -- were never put to the binary at all, so the true count is higher and no instrument can say by how much.

=== WHY THIS IS NOT 0188 ===

0188 is that the register cannot record **why** a row was closed, so no instrument can tell a fix from a wontfix. This is that a row cannot record **which build** it describes. Sibling holes in the same record, different fields, different consequences: 0188 corrupts the CLOSED set, this one corrupts the OPEN set. A row can be perfectly open, perfectly true of `main`, and false of everything anyone has installed.

=== THE CONSEQUENCE THAT IS ALREADY PAID ===

`docs/known-defects.md` exists because of this hole and is maintained by hand against it. Its *NOT present* section is pure compensation: prose written to stop a reader being alarmed by an open issue that describes a version they are not on. **That section is a hand-maintained index into a field the register should carry**, and it goes stale the moment anyone files or fixes anything -- which is the shape of a defect being paid for in documentation rather than fixed.

=== A CORRECTION I OWE, RECORDED HERE BECAUSE IT IS THE SAME CLASS ===

I handed this finding to vc as **twenty-one** rows, and as filed under **0188**. Both were wrong and vc caught the second one. Checking it produced the first: **21 is not reproducible from any artefact in the estate.** The durable record derives ten; the per-member manifest (`ac0203-dispositions.tsv`) carries only `stated | not-reader-reachable` and no present-or-absent verdict, so the count I quoted was never derivable from it. `21` appears to have been carried across from `0080`'s unrelated *21 of 56*.

**The figure lived on a board and in a handover and in no instrument.** That is the whole mechanism: a number with no home that derives it survives on restatement alone, and every restatement makes it look better sourced. The ten above is stated with the command that produces it so the next reader re-derives rather than inherits.
